title: Cloudflare’s Post-Quantum GeoKey Manager Enters Closed Beta Without Attribute-Based Encryption
gist: Cloudflare moved a post-quantum rebuild of GeoKey Manager into closed beta on October 23, replacing the attribute-based encryption used since 2022 with HPKE using hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519, regional root keys and epoch-based rotation, with GA planned for Q1 2027. The design deliberately fails closed, raising the open question of whether customers will accept region-wide outages when key provisioning fails.

insights.claim: Cloudflare's post-quantum GeoKey Manager entered closed beta on October 23 for existing Data Localization Suite customers, with general availability planned for Q1 2027.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Timeline marker for Cloudflare's sovereignty/PQC product roadmap.
insights.locator: Cloudflare has moved a post-quantum rebuild

insights.claim: Cloudflare frames the GeoKey Manager redesign as solving two demands at once: data-sovereignty rules confining plaintext processing to a region, and harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks where traffic captured today is decrypted once quantum computers exist.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Sovereignty regulation plus quantum risk are converging budget drivers for edge-security vendors.
insights.locator: Chetan Agrawal, Arka Nayan and Erik Engstrom

insights.claim: Cloudflare dropped the ciphertext-policy attribute-based encryption GeoKey Manager used since 2022 because no production-ready post-quantum variant exists and customers don't need the large number of regions it was built to express.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Shows PQC migration forces abandonment of exotic crypto schemes in favor of standardized primitives.

insights.claim: The new GeoKey Manager uses HPKE (RFC 9180) with a hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519 KEM, HKDF-SHA-256 and AES-256-GCM, with 256-bit regional root keys and application key pairs derived per service (e.g., Tunnel, Gateway) and per epoch.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Hybrid ML-KEM is becoming the de facto industry PQC pattern.
insights.locator: In its place, key protection uses HPKE

insights.claim: Cloudflare adopted hybrid ML-KEM for its IPsec service in March, when over 60% of human-generated TLS traffic on its network already used it, and has set out plans for a quantum-safe certificate authority.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Majority of Cloudflare human TLS traffic is already PQ-protected, indicating PQC adoption is mainstream at the edge.

insights.claim: Before a Cloudflare edge server receives a regional root key it must pass TPM hardware identity verification, a Zinc server-inventory lookup mapping it to a data center and location, and a provisioning-service decision; keys are stored in Vault and loaded into the volatile kernel keyring, so a restart removes them.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Hardware-rooted, location-attested key distribution is the template for credible data-localization claims.
insights.quote: a machine restart removes the keys
insights.locator: The two kinds of keys travel different paths

insights.claim: Cloudflare's globally replicated Quicksilver store carries only wrapped keys and metadata and sits outside the GeoKey trust boundary, which covers only key-management, provisioning and authorized edge key services.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Narrow trust boundary limits blast radius if the global replication layer is compromised.

insights.claim: GeoKey Manager rotates keys via epochs: soft rotation creates a new epoch while a limited number of prior epochs remain usable to preserve uptime; hard rotation rewraps affected keys and removes access to the previous epoch.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Answers enterprise concern about zero-downtime rotation of geo-fenced keys.
insights.locator: Dabeer Shaikh, a senior solutions engineer

insights.claim: GeoKey Manager rejects any request failing service-context, region or epoch checks, and edge services refuse to start with a missing or malformed key, which Cloudflare calls a very intentional design choice.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Fail-closed design trades availability for sovereignty guarantees; a provisioning bug could become a regional Cloudflare outage.

insights.claim: Cybersecurity professor Mark Tehrani questioned whether fail-closed GeoKey provisioning failures could cause region-wide outages and whether a compromised Zinc inventory or control plane could hand regional keys to out-of-region servers; InfoQ says the beta will test whether customers accept refuse-to-serve at regional scale.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Monitor beta feedback and any GeoKey-related incidents before GA in Q1 2027.
insights.quote: If regional key provisioning, synchronization, or rotation fails, could the fail-closed design cause a region-wide service outage?
